pr_title: benchmark: remove dependency on unshipped tools
pr_body:

Fixes: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/51145

comments: Seems this is kind of test regression introduced in https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/50684 where this tests relies on this removed tool. `tools/node_modules` are removed from the tarball for some time, meaning many years.
Ideally this should have been caught by the https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/.github/workflows/build-tarball.yml workflow in https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/50684 but it was not 😞.

```
      - name: Copy directories needed for testing
        run: |
          cp -r tools/node_modules $TAR_DIR/tools
          cp -r tools/eslint-rules $TAR_DIR/tools
```
this seems to copy things over :thinking: I think either these should be then shipped or should not be needed for tests?
I'm not sure it's reasonable to expect that benchmarks and their tests work with the release tarball.

Well, it's been working since at least nodejs 4.x :wink:  I'm happy if `tools/node_modules` is removed in tarball, but there is no `package-lock.json` that allows it to be installed again. This removed part of tarball is about 22MB of disk space.

The `tools/eslint-rules` are only 100kB so this can be added to the tarball.

review_comments: I think we can simply test its existence with `fs.existsSync()` when creating the benchmark and only add it to the array when it exists (i.e. in dev mode). `tools/node_modules` exist when developers clone the repo and run `make lint-js`, just not in the release tarball.
Yes, this could be another option here. I'll adjust this patch
